diatonicChords.function: Tonic - Bright major tonic with a floating, unresolved quality from the #4
Supertonic - Characteristic Lydian chord, the major II creates the dreamy brightness
Mediant - Minor chord providing emotional depth and contrast
Subdominant - Diminished chord built on the characteristic #4, adds tension
Dominant - Standard dominant function with strong resolution tendency
Submediant - Relative minor for emotional coloring
Leading Tone - Minor leading tone chord, gentle pull toward tonic

practiceExercises.name: C Lydian Scale Runs
practiceExercises.description: Practice the C Lydian scale ascending and descending, focusing on the characteristic #4 (F#) that distinguishes it from C major
instructions: Start slowly with metronome at 60 BPM
Listen for the F# that gives Lydian its bright, floating quality
Compare with C major to hear how the single raised 4th transforms the sound

practiceExercises.name: Lydian Chord Tone Targeting
practiceExercises.description: Practice targeting the #4 and major 7th chord tones over Lydian vamps to develop authentic modal phrasing
instructions: Play over a C-D major chord vamp (I-II progression)
Emphasize the F# on strong beats to highlight the Lydian character
Resolve phrases to the root and major 3rd for stability

practiceExercises.name: Lydian vs Major Ear Training
practiceExercises.description: Compare Lydian with the major scale to hear the characteristic #4 that creates the dreamy, floating quality
instructions: Play C Lydian, then C major (Ionian) back to back
Focus on the 4th degree difference (F# vs F natural in C)
Sing both scales to internalize the bright, uplifting Lydian character

relatedScales.differences: Lydian has a raised 4th instead of natural 4th - this is the only difference
relatedScales.usage: Standard major sound without the floating Lydian brightness

relatedScales.differences: Lydian dominant has a flat 7th in addition to the sharp 4th, combining brightness with a dominant character
relatedScales.usage: Jazz and fusion contexts, resolving dominant 7th #11 chords

relatedScales.differences: Mixolydian has a flat 7th creating a bluesy dominant sound; Lydian has a sharp 4th creating a bright dreamy sound
relatedScales.usage: Earthier, more grounded major mode for blues, rock, and country
